topm-01-c2.text: Markus König, Steffen Wiedmann, Christoph Brüne, Andreas Roth, Hartmut Buhmann, Laurens W. Molenkamp, Xiao-Liang Qi, Shou-Cheng Zhang (2007). Quantum Spin Hall Insulator State in HgTe Quantum Wells. Science 318, 766–770.
topm-01-c2.quote: The quantum phase transition at the critical thickness, d = 6.3 nm,
topm-01-c2.claim: Thin wells inherit CdTe ordering (trivial), thick wells inherit HgTe ordering (topological), with a phase transition at dc ≈ 6.3 nm

topm-01-c3.text: Y. Xia, D. Qian, D. Hsieh, L. Wray, A. Pal, H. Lin, A. Bansil, D. Grauer, Y. S. Hor, R. J. Cava, M. Z. Hasan (2009). Observation of a large-gap topological-insulator class with a single Dirac cone on the surface. Nature Physics 5, 398–402.
topm-01-c3.quote: have nearly equal band velocities, approximately 5×10⁵ ms⁻¹, along the two directions
topm-01-c3.claim: a single Dirac cone inside the gap, dispersing as E = ℏvF|k| with vF ≈ 5 × 10⁵ m/s

topm-02-c1.text: Liang Fu, C. L. Kane, E. J. Mele (2007). Topological Insulators in Three Dimensions. Physical Review Letters 98, 106803 (arXiv).
topm-02-c1.quote: in three dimensions there are 4 invariants distinguishing 16 "topological insulator" phases.
topm-02-c1.claim: A 3D time-reversal-invariant insulator is classified by four Z₂ invariants (ν0; ν1ν2ν3), introduced by Fu, Kane, and Mele in 2007.

topm-03-c1.text: B. Andrei Bernevig, Taylor L. Hughes, Shou-Cheng Zhang (2006). Quantum Spin Hall Effect and Topological Phase Transition in HgTe Quantum Wells. Science 314, 1757 (arXiv).
topm-03-c1.quote: We show that the Quantum Spin Hall Effect, a state of matter with topological properties distinct from conventional insulators, can be realized in HgTe/CdTe semiconductor quantum wells.
topm-03-c1.claim: In 2006 Bernevig, Hughes, and Zhang proposed a precise materials prediction: a HgTe layer of thickness above a critical value dc, sandwiched between CdTe barriers, would realize the 2D quantum spin Hall state.

topm-03-c2.text: Markus König, Steffen Wiedmann, Christoph Brüne, Andreas Roth, Hartmut Buhmann, Laurens W. Molenkamp, Xiao-Liang Qi, Shou-Cheng Zhang (2007). Quantum Spin Hall Insulator State in HgTe Quantum Wells. Science (arXiv).
topm-03-c2.quote: Furthermore, the residual conductance is destroyed by a small external magnetic field.
topm-03-c2.claim: First, applying an in-plane magnetic field, which breaks the TRS protecting the helical edge, opened a gap and destroyed the plateau.

topm-05-c1.text: Timothy H. Hsieh, Hsin Lin, Junwei Liu, Wenhui Duan, Arun Bansil, Liang Fu (2012). Topological Crystalline Insulators in the SnTe Material Class. Nature Communications 3, 982 (arXiv).
topm-05-c1.quote: Here we predict the first material realization of topological crystalline insulator in the semiconductor SnTe, by identifying its nonzero topological index.
topm-05-c1.claim: The first experimental realization was the SnTe family (SnTe, Pb1−xSnxTe, Pb1−xSnxSe) predicted by Hsieh, Lin, Liu, Duan, Bansil, and Fu (2012) and confirmed by ARPES on (001) surfaces in 2012.

topm-05-c2.text: Wladimir A. Benalcazar, B. Andrei Bernevig, Taylor L. Hughes (2017). Quantized electric multipole insulators. Science 357, 61 (arXiv).
topm-05-c2.quote: We determine the necessary conditions under which, and minimal models in which, the quadrupole and octupole moments are topologically quantized electromagnetic observables.
topm-05-c2.claim: The framework (quantized quadrupole, octupole, and bulk multipole moments) was developed by Benalcazar, Bernevig, and Hughes (Science 2017).

topm-06-c3.text: Lukasz Fidkowski, Alexei Kitaev (2010). Topological phases of fermions in one dimension. Physical Review B 83, 075103 (arXiv).
topm-06-c3.quote: Here we show that the eight equivalence classes are distinct and exhaustive, and provide a physical interpretation for the interacting invariant modulo 8.
topm-06-c3.claim: The first example was Fidkowski and Kitaev (2010): the BDI ℤ classification in 1D, counting Majorana zero modes at each end of a class-BDI superconducting wire, collapses to ℤ₈ under generic four-fermion interactions.

topm-02-c3.text: Cui-Zu Chang et al (2013). Experimental Observation of the Quantum Anomalous Hall Effect in a Magnetic Topological Insulator. Science 340, 167 (arXiv).
topm-02-c3.quote: Here, we report the observation of the quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect in thin films of Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3, a magnetic topological insulator.
topm-02-c3.claim: Chang et al. observed this first in 2013 at T ~ 30 mK

topm-04-c3.text: D. T. Son, B. Z. Spivak (2013). Chiral Anomaly and Classical Negative Magnetoresistance of Weyl Metals. Physical Review B 88, 104412 (arXiv).
topm-04-c3.quote: Such a system may exhibit large negative magnetoresistance with unusual anisotropy as a function of the angle between the electric and magnetic fields.
topm-04-c3.claim: The transport consequence, derived by Son and Spivak (2013), is a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance when B ∥ I.
